summary: A wide sunlit countryside where the sky is the subject: flat cloud banks, grouped green value masses and one terracotta accent, painted rather than simulated.
objective: The sky fills at least 45% of frame height and holds the brightest value in the frame; foliage reads as three to five painted value bands per canopy at the intended output size, not as individual leaves.
intent_signals: Studio Ghibli style countryside with big clouds
Miyazaki-like painted sky over a meadow
Hand-painted animation background feel, not photoreal
example_prompts: A hillside meadow under towering summer clouds with one red-roofed cottage, painterly and hand-painted in feel.
Wide pastoral valley with a grass path, wind through the field and a painted sky.

principles: This is a painterly pastoral look inspired by the shared traits of hand-painted animation backgrounds; it does not require imitating, reproducing or crediting any named studio, film or artist, and no such name is part of the recipe.

Triangulate three traits shared by hand-painted animation backgrounds — (a) the sky is a designed subject with its own composition rather than a backdrop, (b) foliage and ground are grouped into a few painted value masses instead of per-element detail, (c) a single warm man-made accent anchors an otherwise green-and-blue field. Take those three traits; no named film or artist is a requirement.

Silhouette rule: two hill masses cross at different heights so the horizon is never a single straight line, and one vertical element (a lone tree, a pole, a chimney) breaks the horizon at roughly the one-third mark.
Scale cues, always present: door height 2.0 m, fence post 1.1 m, mature tree 9-14 m, and grass blades sized so a standing figure would clear them by 1.2 m.
The shadow floor stays above 0.12 luminance — hand-painted daylight has coloured shadows (sky-blue bounce), never black ones.
implementation: Sky: gradient dome from #2f5f9e at zenith to #cfe3ef at horizon, plus cumulus banks modelled as flat card layers at three depths — 30 m, 120 m and 600 m — each with a 2-value paint (lit #fdfbf4, underside #cfe3ef) and no volumetric scattering.

Foliage: 3-5 flat value bands per canopy, 6% hue jitter and 8% scale jitter per instance on an InstancedMesh, and per-instance rotation so no two trees share a silhouette; canopies are read as masses, so keep polygon detail under 400 triangles per tree at mid distance.
Wind: vertex-shader sway with a 4.0-6.5 s period, 2.5° amplitude on grass and 1.2° on canopies, phase offset by world x so the field ripples as one wave instead of shivering in place.

Key light at 52° elevation, azimuth 135°, colour #fff2d8 at intensity 3.0 with castShadow true; hemisphere fill #8fb8e0 over #6b6a45 at 0.9 keeps shadows blue rather than black; a cool 0.5 rim at 20°/315° separates the hill edges from the sky.
Fog: FogExp2 #cfe3ef at density 0.012 — light enough to keep the meadow crisp, strong enough that the far ridge sits a full value lighter than the near one.
Ground albedo is painted in four masses (sunlit meadow, shaded meadow, path, exposed earth); resist per-blade texture detail, since the look comes from the value grouping, not the resolution.
observable_checks: Grayscale screenshot: the cloud highlights are the only region above 0.9, and the darkest shadow never falls below 0.12.
Squint or downsample to 128 px: the frame resolves into four to six value masses, not into noise.
Turn off wind: the composition still reads; turn it on and the whole field moves as one travelling wave rather than as independent jitter.
Count hue families: blue sky, green field and one terracotta accent — a fourth saturated hue means the palette has drifted.

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at renderer.toneMappingExposure 1.05 with three.js physically-based light units; re-tune every intensity under AgX, Neutral or a different exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Time of day is movable: keep the value grouping and drop the key to 20° elevation with a #ffcf9a tint for a late-afternoon variant without touching the material ranges.
The same grouping discipline carries an interior — a sunlit kitchen with four value masses and one warm accent reads from the identical palette logic.
The recipe never dictates subject matter: farms, coastal cliffs, rail sidings or a schoolyard all fit as long as the sky keeps its 45% of frame height and its own composition.

defaults.rationale: The look lives or dies on value grouping, so the numbers are chosen to suppress detail and protect the sky: fog density is a deliberately low 0.012 (a pastoral field must stay crisp while the far ridge lifts one value), and the hemisphere fill runs high at 0.9 against a 3.0 key — a 3.5:1 ratio — so shadows are blue-filled rather than black, which is the single most recognisable trait of hand-painted daylight. Bloom threshold sits at 1.1 with only 0.15 strength because the cumulus highlight at #fdfbf4 should be the brightest value without smearing into a glow, and exposure 1.05 keeps the mids open where the painted bands live.

palette.role: horizon haze, cloud underside, fog colour
terracotta accent (roof, cloth, single man-made mass)

values.value_structure: 30/50/20 dark/mid/light; sky occupies ≥ 45% of frame height and carries the lightest mass
values.saturation_rule: greens ≤ 50% HSL saturation; the single terracotta accent ≤ 65%; clouds under 8% saturation

lights.ratio: key:fill ≈ 3.5:1 on a neutral card; shadow floor never below 0.12 luminance

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: no specular hot spots anywhere; canopies painted as 3-5 flat value bands with 6% hue and 8% scale jitter per instance; ground albedo authored as four masses (sunlit meadow, shaded meadow, path, bare earth) rather than per-blade texture

values.signature_technique: Cumulus banks built as flat card layers at 30 m, 120 m and 600 m with the fog colour equal to the horizon, so the sky reads as a painted composition with its own depth rather than as a simulated volume.
never: a uniform grid of identical trees
